title: Retrospective paired pointwise loss comparison with whole-galaxy inference
status: specified before new bootstrap outcomes; existing data and model development already explored
primary_sample: all131 galaxies and659 original outer rows; no refit or model selection
primary_loss: pointwise squared standardized residual z^2, averaged within galaxy, then equal weight per galaxy
primary_effect: mean across galaxies of envelope-minus-comparator loss; negative favors envelope
primary_se: sample standard deviation of galaxy mean differences divided by sqrt(G)
ci: 95% whole-galaxy pairs bootstrap-t interval; percentile interval retained as sensitivity
test: two-sided null-imposed studentized wild cluster bootstrap, independent Rademacher multipliers on full galaxy difference scores, intercept null mean0
p: (1+tail_count)/(B+1), report Monte Carlo tail count and Clopper-Pearson interval; never zero
multiplicity: Holm4 for the four declared new mean-loss tests only
Z: unsigned two-sided Gaussian probability equivalent from Holm4 p; at simulation floor mark finite resolution, do not extrapolate
assumptions: independent galaxy clusters for sampling inference, enough non-dominant clusters; arbitrary radial dependence retained by whole-galaxy resampling; not exact sign randomization under a mean-only null

sensitivities.weighting: pooled-point ratio of sums, whole-galaxy resampled with denominator recomputed
robust_scores: mean absolute velocity error in km/s
sensitivities.correlated_score: common assumed standardized-error equicorrelation matrix, quadratic form per point; no rho fitting or selection
sensitivities.influence: every leave-one-galaxy-out mean, effective variance-contribution count, maximum variance share; no deletions from primary

profiled_baryons: retain one failed training case as failure; full continuous mean comparison not finite; all-feasible130 subset separately labelled sensitivity, with no primary p
adaptive: retain saved data for provenance; no new primary test
limitations: conditional on saved fitted curves, no refit uncertainty or covariance estimation, no fresh validation, no model-history multiplicity correction, no naive chi-square difference/Wilks/AIC/Bayes-factor claims
